hook.text: Checkmate in 4 moves. Beginners fall for this all the time.

step-0.text: Pawn to e4. This opens the door for our queen and bishop.

step-1.text: Black copies us. Totally normal.

step-2.text: Bishop out. It's aiming at f7.

step-3.text: Look at f7. Only the king protects it. That's the weak spot!

step-4.text: Black brings out a knight. Looks fine...

step-5.text: Queen out! Now two pieces attack f7.

step-6.text: Black attacks our queen... But forgets about f7!

step-7.text: Queen takes f7. The bishop protects her. Checkmate!

takeaway-0.text: Queen and bishop attack f7.

takeaway-1.text: If they forget to defend it: Game over.

takeaway-2.text: Playing Black? Stop it with g6 or queen e7.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: The fastest checkmate in chess. Only 2 moves. Seriously.

step-0.text: White pushes the f-pawn. That pawn was guarding the king.

step-1.text: We push our pawn. Now our queen can come out.

step-2.text: White pushes another pawn. Huge mistake.

step-3.text: Look at this line to the king. Nothing is blocking it!

step-4.text: Queen to h4. The king is trapped. Checkmate!

takeaway-0.text: Don't push your f and g pawns early.

takeaway-1.text: They are your king's bodyguards.

takeaway-2.text: Open line to the king means danger.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: They have a queen. We have a rook. We still win in 1 move.

step-0.text: Black has a queen. Black is winning... Right?

step-1.text: Look at their king. It's stuck behind its own pawns. No exit!

step-2.text: Black gets greedy and grabs a pawn.

step-3.text: Rook to the back row. The king can't escape. Checkmate!

takeaway-0.text: King with no exit squares? Look at the back row.

takeaway-1.text: One rook can end the game.

takeaway-2.text: Protect yourself: Give your king one free square (like h6).

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: Give away your queen... And checkmate 2 moves later.

step-0.text: Normal start. Our knight attacks e5.

step-1.text: Black protects it with a pawn.

step-2.text: Bishop out. Aiming at f7, the weak spot.

step-3.text: Black pins our knight. 'If it moves, I take your queen!'

step-4.text: We bring out a piece. Black plays a slow move. Now the trap is ready.

step-5.text: Knight takes e5! We leave our queen to die!

step-6.text: Black grabs the queen. Big mistake.

step-8.text: The king has only one square to go.

step-9.text: Knight to d5. Checkmate! Three small pieces beat a queen.

takeaway-0.text: A pin to the queen is not a real pin.

takeaway-1.text: Sometimes giving the queen wins the game.

takeaway-2.text: Free queen? First check for checkmate.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: This move looks like a blunder... But it ends in checkmate.

step-0.text: Normal opening. White's bishop eyes f7.

step-1.text: Knight to d4. Risky! Now our e5 pawn looks free.

step-2.text: White takes the free pawn. Here we go.

step-3.text: Queen to g5! She attacks the knight and the g2 pawn.

step-4.text: White gets greedy. Knight takes f7, hitting our rook.

step-5.text: We don't care! Queen takes g2. Now their rook is attacked.

step-9.text: Knight to f3. The bishop can't take: It's pinned. Checkmate!

takeaway-0.text: If they grab e5, play queen g5!

takeaway-1.text: Ignore the knight. Attack g2.

takeaway-2.text: Knight d4 is risky. It works when they grab e5.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: White takes our queen... And gets checkmated right away.

step-0.text: White takes our e5 pawn.

step-1.text: We give away a pawn on purpose. The Stafford Gambit!

step-2.text: Trade. Now our bishops have open lines.

step-3.text: Bishop to c5. It's aiming at f2.

step-4.text: White pins our knight to the queen. Looks scary.

step-5.text: We move it anyway! Knight takes e4. Take my queen!

step-8.text: The king has only one square.

takeaway-0.text: Bishop on c5 means pressure on f2.

takeaway-1.text: Pinned to the queen? You can still move.

takeaway-2.text: Before taking a queen, check for checks.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: White takes a free pawn. 6 moves later: Checkmate.

step-0.text: We throw a pawn at them. The Englund Gambit.

step-1.text: White takes and protects it.

step-2.text: Queen to e7. We attack e5 again.

step-3.text: White protects it one more time.

step-4.text: Queen to b4. Check! And she's eyeing b2.

step-5.text: We take b2. Now we attack the rook in the corner.

step-6.text: White attacks our queen. This is the mistake.

step-7.text: Bishop to b4! Their bishop is now pinned.

step-9.text: We take the bishop. Our queen doesn't care.

step-10.text: White takes back... And walks into it.

takeaway-0.text: Gambit means give a pawn to attack fast.

takeaway-1.text: Pin pieces to the king with your bishop.

takeaway-2.text: Every move, ask: What are their checks?

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: White thinks they won a pawn. Really, they just lost a piece.

step-0.text: The Queen's Gambit. Very normal stuff.

step-1.text: White pins our knight to the queen.

step-2.text: Knight to d7. This quietly sets the trap.

step-3.text: Pawns trade on d5.

step-4.text: White grabs d5. 'Your knight is pinned!' they think.

step-5.text: Surprise! We take anyway and give our queen.

step-9.text: We take their queen with check.

step-10.text: And we take the bishop. We're a whole piece up!

takeaway-0.text: A pinned knight can still move.

takeaway-1.text: Lose your queen, take theirs and a piece.

takeaway-2.text: Free pawn? Count the checks first.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: White takes our bishop. Next move: Checkmate.

step-0.text: We give a pawn. The Budapest Gambit.

step-1.text: Our knights attack e5.

step-2.text: White protects it with the bishop.

step-3.text: Bishop check!

step-4.text: White blocks with the knight.

step-5.text: Queen to e7. Now three pieces hit e5.

step-7.text: We ignore it and take e5! Leave the bishop.

step-9.text: Look: The e2 pawn is pinned. The king is boxed in.

takeaway-0.text: Pin the e2 pawn with your queen.

takeaway-1.text: King boxed in by its own pieces means knight mate.

takeaway-2.text: Free bishop? Check for mate first.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: Promote a pawn to a knight? Yes. And it wins the queen.

step-0.text: We give a pawn. The Albin Countergambit.

step-1.text: Our pawn pushes forward. Annoying for White.

step-2.text: White attacks it. This is the mistake.

step-3.text: Bishop check!

step-4.text: We take on e3. Now we hit f2 and the bishop.

step-5.text: White takes our bishop. Big mistake.

step-8.text: Pawn takes the knight and becomes... A knight! With check!

step-9.text: Why a knight? A queen gives no check. The knight does.

step-11.text: Bishop check! And it hits the queen.

step-12.text: The king steps back... And we take their queen!

takeaway-0.text: Promote to a knight when it gives check.

takeaway-1.text: Checks first, captures second.

takeaway-2.text: Against the Albin, avoid e3.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: Throw your knight as bait... And catch a checkmate.

step-0.text: The Roo-ee Lopez. White castles. Very normal.

step-1.text: Knight to g4. Risky... But it's our fishing pole!

step-2.text: White kicks the knight.

step-3.text: We leave it there. The knight is the bait.

step-4.text: White takes the free knight...

step-5.text: We take back. Now the h-file is wide open.

step-7.text: Queen to h4. Threat: Queen to h1 is mate!

step-8.text: White makes room for the king.

step-9.text: Pawn to g3. Now nothing can stop mate.

takeaway-0.text: Taking the bait opens the h-file.

takeaway-1.text: Rook and queen on an open file means mate.

takeaway-2.text: Risky trap: It only works if they take the bait.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: Their queen looks safe. One knight jump: Checkmate.

step-0.text: White gives a pawn to attack. The Smith-Morra Gambit.

step-1.text: We take it. Everyone develops.

step-2.text: Queen to c7. Look at her diagonal.

step-3.text: White castles. Our knight comes out.

step-4.text: Knight to g4. Now two pieces hit h2.

step-6.text: White kicks our knight. Natural... But wrong!

step-7.text: Knight to d4! It attacks the queen.

step-8.text: White takes it... But now nobody guards h2.

takeaway-0.text: Queen and knight versus h2 means danger.

takeaway-1.text: Kill or distract the defender.

takeaway-2.text: Attack two things at once.

cta.text: How to defend it? It's in the next video. Follow so you don't miss it!

hook.text: They want mate in 4. Here's how to stop it.

step-0.text: Normal start. But watch that bishop on c4.

step-1.text: Queen out! Threat: Queen takes f7, checkmate!

step-2.text: Pawn to g6! It kicks the queen away.

step-3.text: The queen comes back. Same threat on f7!

step-4.text: Knight to f6 blocks it. F7 is safe!

step-5.text: Now we attack the bishop. Their queen came out too early.

takeaway-0.text: Queen on h5? Play g6.

takeaway-1.text: Queen on f3? Block with knight f6.

takeaway-2.text: Early queen means easy target.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: Never lose to the fastest mate. Just follow one rule.

step-0.text: We pushed the f-pawn. Not great, but not lost.

step-1.text: Black's queen now eyes h4. Our king is open.

step-2.text: Pushing the g-pawn now is checkmate. Don't do it!

step-3.text: Play e4 instead. If the queen checks, g3 blocks.

step-4.text: Bring out pieces. Keep the king safe.

takeaway-0.text: Keep your f and g pawns home early.

takeaway-1.text: Start with e4 or d4, then knights.

takeaway-2.text: Open line to your king? Close it.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: Winning? Don't lose to one rook. One tiny move saves you.

step-0.text: We have a queen. We're winning!

step-1.text: But our king has no exit. Its own pawns block it.

step-2.text: Rook to d8 would be checkmate.

step-3.text: So first: Pawn to h6. Now the king can breathe.

step-4.text: Rook check on the back row...

step-5.text: No problem. The king escapes to h7!

takeaway-0.text: King stuck on the back row means danger.

takeaway-1.text: Make one escape square (h6 or g6).

takeaway-2.text: Then grab material safely.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: They try Lay-gahl's Mate... And just lose their queen.

step-0.text: We pin their knight to the queen.

step-1.text: Here, don't play g6. That's when the trap works.

step-2.text: Knight to f6! It guards d5 and g4.

step-3.text: White tries the trick anyway: Knight takes e5!

step-4.text: This time, take the queen!

step-5.text: Bishop check. King to e7, like before...

step-6.text: Knight check... But that square is covered!

step-7.text: Our knight takes it. No mate. We're a queen up!

takeaway-0.text: Pinned their knight? Play knight f6 next.

takeaway-1.text: Guard d5 and the trap dies.

takeaway-2.text: Never play g6 there.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: That free pawn is poison. Do this instead.

step-0.text: Normal opening.

step-1.text: Black plays knight d4. Now e5 looks free...

step-2.text: If we take it, queen g5 starts a deadly attack.

step-3.text: Instead, take the knight!

step-4.text: Then castle. We're safe and better.

takeaway-0.text: Knight on d4? Take it, not e5.

takeaway-1.text: Free pawns can be poison.

takeaway-2.text: Castle early, stay safe.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: Beat the Stafford Gambit. Just don't play this move.

step-0.text: Black gives a pawn: The Stafford Gambit.

step-1.text: Their bishop now aims at f2.

step-2.text: Don't pin with bishop g5. That's exactly the trap!

step-3.text: Bishop to e2. It guards g4 and our king.

step-4.text: Black attacks f2 anyway...

step-5.text: Just take the knight. We're a piece up!

takeaway-0.text: Against the Stafford: Bishop e2, not bishop g5.

takeaway-1.text: Guard f2 and g4.

takeaway-2.text: Then castle and stay calm.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: Took the Englund pawn? One knight move wins.

step-0.text: The Englund Gambit. We grabbed a pawn.

step-1.text: Black's queen grabs b2 and hits our rook.

step-2.text: Bishop c3 loses here! It gets pinned, then mate.

step-3.text: Knight to c3! Next, our rook hunts the queen.

step-4.text: Rook attacks the queen. She must run.

step-5.text: Our knight jumps in. Black is in trouble.

takeaway-0.text: Queen on b2? Play knight c3, then rook b1.

takeaway-1.text: Never bishop c3 there: It gets pinned.

takeaway-2.text: Chase the greedy queen!

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: D5 looks free. It's not. Here's the safe move.

step-0.text: The Queen's Gambit. We pin their knight.

step-1.text: Pawns trade. Now d5 looks free.

step-2.text: But knight takes d5 loses a piece! Their knight isn't really pinned.

step-3.text: Play e3. Calm and solid.

step-4.text: Develop and castle. Trap dodged.

takeaway-0.text: Pinned to the queen means not fully pinned.

takeaway-1.text: Free pawn? Check what they get.

takeaway-2.text: Solid moves win at your level.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: Avoid a smothered mate... With one pawn move.

step-0.text: The Budapest Gambit.

step-1.text: Black hits e5 three times.

step-2.text: If we play a3, a smothered mate is coming!

step-3.text: Play e3 instead. Our king gets air.

step-4.text: Black wins the pawn back. That's fine.

step-5.text: Develop and castle. No mate here!

takeaway-0.text: Budapest Gambit? Play e3 early.

takeaway-1.text: Don't let your king get boxed in.

takeaway-2.text: A3 there is a trap!

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: The Albin hides a nasty trap. Here's how to dodge it.

step-0.text: The Albin Countergambit.

step-1.text: Their pawn pushes to d4. Annoying.

step-2.text: Attacking it with e3 falls into the trap!

step-3.text: Play knight f3. Just develop.

step-4.text: Knights out. Next one goes to b3.

step-5.text: Now we attack d4 and win it back.

takeaway-0.text: Against the Albin: Knight f3, not e3.

takeaway-1.text: Win the d4 pawn later.

takeaway-2.text: Knights before pawns.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: A free knight? It's bait. Don't bite. Do this.

step-0.text: The Roo-ee Lopez. We castle.

step-1.text: Black leaves the knight hanging...

step-2.text: It's bait! Taking opens the h-file for their rook.

step-3.text: Don't take! Play c3, then d4.

step-4.text: We grab the center. Their knight is still stuck.

takeaway-0.text: Free knight next to your king? Bait.

takeaway-1.text: Don't open the h-file.

takeaway-2.text: Play the center instead.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!

hook.text: Don't kick that knight! Here's the safe move.

step-0.text: We play the Smith-Morra Gambit.

step-1.text: Everyone develops.

step-2.text: Knight to g4. Two pieces hit h2.

step-3.text: Kicking it with h3 loses! Knight d4 is coming.

step-4.text: Rook to d1. Now our queen has f1 to escape.

step-5.text: Knight to b5 kicks their queen.

takeaway-0.text: Knight g4 and queen c7? No h3.

takeaway-1.text: Give your queen an escape square.

takeaway-2.text: Attack their queen first.

cta.text: New trap tomorrow. Follow!
